claims.statement: The repository is a monorepo of independently versioned packages under libs/; there is no root pyproject.toml, and each package carries its own pyproject.toml, Makefile, and README.md so work happens inside the package being changed.

The core packages have distinct responsibilities: deepagents is the SDK (create_deep_agent, middleware, backends), code is the prebuilt terminal coding agent run via dcode, acp is the Agent Client Protocol editor integration, evals is the evaluation suite with Harbor integration, talon is the experimental long-running host, and partners holds provider/sandbox integrations (Daytona, Modal, Runloop, Vercel, QuickJS).

Deep Agents is a three-layer stack: LangGraph is the runtime (state, checkpoints, streaming, interrupts), LangChain's create_agent is the agent abstraction (model + tools + middleware forming the agent loop), and Deep Agents is an opinionated harness on top of create_agent that does not introduce a new runtime.
Local package dependencies within the monorepo are editable, so changes in one package are visible to sibling packages that depend on it during development.

Monorepo development uses uv for interpreters/environments and per-package Makefiles as the source of truth for commands; uv provisions the correct Python interpreter automatically so there is no global Python version to pin.

The manifests declare directional first-party dependencies: deepagents-code pins deepagents==0.7.19; deepagents-acp depends on deepagents; deepagents-evals depends on deepagents, deepagents-code, and Harbor; and deepagents-talon depends on deepagents and deepagents-code.

The core package manifests declare different Python compatibility ranges: deepagents supports >=3.11,<4.0, deepagents-code >=3.12,<4.0, deepagents-acp >=3.11, deepagents-evals >=3.12,<3.14, and deepagents-talon >=3.12; therefore a compatible interpreter must be selected for the package being run, and evals excludes Python 3.14.

The five current partner package manifests (Daytona, Modal, Runloop, Vercel, and QuickJS) each declare Python >=3.11,<4.0 and a first-party deepagents dependency, making them package-local SDK integration boundaries rather than repository-wide requirements.

Release-please baselines are deepagents 0.7.19, deepagents-acp 0.0.12, deepagents-code 0.1.77, deepagents-talon 0.0.8, and the five partner packages Daytona 0.0.8, Modal 0.0.6, Runloop 0.0.7, Vercel 0.0.2, and QuickJS 0.3.7.

The SDK and Code Makefiles accept TEST_FILE for focused unit runs; those targets disable network sockets except Unix sockets, run pytest in parallel, and report missing-line coverage. Code lint also checks the generated command catalog and process current-working-directory rule, while ACP's default test target uses tests/ with a 10-second timeout.
Code's make check runs lint, import checks, unit tests, extras/version consistency checks, a lockfile check, and an advisory SDK-pin check.

Release dependency validation resolves changed release manifests against PyPI after stripping editable local sources, so local development resolution does not prove the published dependency graph resolves.

The SDK-pin workflow warns on a stale Code SDK pin but documents publication as the hard enforcement point; the partner-bounds workflow is advisory and identifies partner deepagents upper bounds that would exclude the SDK release version.
Release Please is configured for separate draft pull requests for nine managed Python package units—SDK, ACP, Code, Talon, and five partner distributions—while evals is not in the release manifest.
The deepagents-code source version is 0.1.77 in both its project metadata and release-managed `_version.py`, matching the `libs/code` Release Please baseline.
Talon's default test target runs its WhatsApp bridge Node tests before running Python tests with sockets disabled except for Unix sockets, a 10-second timeout, and coverage reporting.
Installing the repository pre-commit hooks enables formatting, linting, lockfile, and Conventional Commit validation before commits, with changed-package formatting and linting run by the hooks.

Talon is an experimental local host whose single event loop owns channel adapters, cron schedulers, and the agent runtime; its runtime constructs a Deep Agents graph at startup using resolved tools, approvals, middleware, subagents, backend, memory, and checkpointer configuration.

Talon's persistent scheduler changes should be tested at the focused boundary: cron expression tests cover parsing, calendar extensions, and DST behavior; `until` tests cover expiration and late-run semantics; job and scheduler tests cover stored-job lifecycle, execution outcomes, and delivery.

Talon defines chat commands in a shared registry used by the host and channel adapters; visible entries provide both help text and platform registrations, while hidden commands remain typeable but are excluded from those advertised surfaces.

`/context-doctor` is a read-only diagnostic: it reports estimated configured and current-thread context counts without running the model or exposing private content, and the host dispatch leaves active work uninterrupted.
